entries.title: C0052 exact source target: subcritical renormalized coupling
entries.statement: HISTORICAL CONJECTURE; current openness UNKNOWN. For the free zero-field nearest-neighbour Ising state on Z^3 at 0<beta<beta_c, let G_beta(x)=E[sigma_0 sigma_x], chi=sum_x G_beta(x), xi=[lim_n -(1/n) log G_beta(n e1)]^{-1}, and U4 be the four-spin expectation minus its three Wick pairings. With the source convention g(beta)=sum_{x,y,z}U4(0,x,y,z)/(chi^2 xi^3)<=0, prove that g(beta) does not tend to zero as beta increases to beta_c. This is PIMS 2017, arXiv:1707.00520v1, equations 7.1-7.2 and Conjecture 6, printed p94. Critical smeared-field cumulants use a different normalization; no equivalence is assumed here.
assumptions: nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic Ising model on Z^3
free zero-field subcritical state
chi and exponential xi finite at each beta<beta_c
historical statement only; not solved here

entries.title: Scope and direction of the original-current Ursell identity
entries.statement: ATTRIBUTED INPUT: for a finite free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model, U4(x,y,z,t)=-2 G(x,y)G(z,t) P^{xy,zt}(x connected to z in n+m), where n and m are independent single currents, source labels cancel modulo two, and connectivity to oneself is permitted. The infinite-volume version at beta<=beta_c uses the no-infinite-path/continuity input in Aizenman-Duminil-Copin arXiv:1912.07973v4 section 3.2. Its equation 3.13 compares this probability from ABOVE by the overlap probability of independently enlarged clusters after adding sourceless currents. A lower bound on that enlarged-cluster probability alone is insufficient for a lower bound on the original probability.
assumptions: free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model
current weights proportional to product J_e^n_e/n_e!
independent currents with specified parity source sets
infinite-volume extension requires the primary source's additional input

entries.title: Conditional fourth-moment deficit witness
entries.statement: Let X_n converge in law to X, E X_n=0, E X_n^2=1, and let |X_n|^4 be uniformly integrable. If liminf_n(3-E X_n^4)>=epsilon>0, then E X=0, E X^2=1, E X^4<=3-epsilon, and X is non-Gaussian.
entries.proof_text: Truncate the first, second and fourth powers continuously. Weak convergence handles bounded truncations, and uniform integrability controls tails for the sequence and its limit. Thus all three moments converge. A centered variance-one Gaussian has fourth moment three, contrary to the positive deficit.
assumptions: distributional convergence
centered variance-one variables
uniform integrability of fourth powers
positive liminf deficit

entries.title: Exact block cumulant under variance-weighted sources
entries.statement: In a finite connected free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model with positive edge couplings, choose nonzero nonnegative weights a, M=sum_x a_x sigma_x, V=E M^2, and ordered endpoints with rho(x,y)=a_x a_y G(x,y)/V. Independently draw two endpoint pairs (X,Y),(Z,T) from rho and single currents n,m sourced at the respective pairs, cancelling repeated labels modulo two. Then 3-E[(M/sqrt(V))^4]=2 P(X connected to Z in n+m), including repeated endpoints.
entries.proof_text: Expand the fourth cumulant as a finite weighted sum of U4. Each Wick pairing sums to V^2. Insert the original-current identity and divide by V^2; the coefficient becomes rho(x,y)rho(z,t). Keep every repeated-label term using parity source cancellation.
assumptions: finite connected graph with positive ferromagnetic couplings
free zero-field state
finite nonnegative weights not all zero
independent pair draws and currents
original-current Ursell identity with parity cancellation

entries.title: A sufficient second moment for single-current source overlap
entries.statement: Under the endpoint law of the variance-weighted cumulant identity, let C and C' be the independent SINGLE-current source clusters, W a finite vertex set, I=|W intersect C intersect C'|, q(v)=P(v in C), q(v,w)=P(v,w in C), A=sum_{v in W}q(v)^2>0, and B=sum_{v,w in W}q(v,w)^2. Then 3-E[(M/sqrt(V))^4]>=2A^2/B. A uniform upper bound B/A^2<=K would therefore provide a uniform deficit of at least 2/K. The ratio bound is an unproved extra input for critical 3D Ising.
entries.proof_text: Independence of the two clusters gives E I=A and E I^2=B. A common vertex connects the two source roots in the union current. Cauchy-Schwarz gives P(I>0)>=A^2/B; combine with the exact cumulant identity.
assumptions: all hypotheses and sampling conventions of the variance-weighted identity
independence between the two marked SINGLE currents
finite W and A>0
no independence of two occupancies within one current

entries.title: Divergent mean overlap with vanishing intersection probability
entries.statement: For integer K>=2 and N=K^3 vertices, independently draw C,C' to be the whole set with probability 1/K and otherwise one uniform vertex. They are independent, identically distributed and nonempty. For I=|C intersect C'|, P(I>0)=2/K-1/K^2+(1-1/K)^2/K^3 ->0, E I=K+2(1-1/K)/K+(1-1/K)^2/K^3 ->infinity, and E I^2=K^4+2(1-1/K)/K+(1-1/K)^2/K^3. Hence E I^2/(E I)^2 is asymptotic to K^2. This refutes a general first-moment inference, not the Ising conjecture.
entries.proof_text: Both sets full has probability 1/K^2 and gives I=N. Exactly one full has probability 2(1-1/K)/K and gives I=1. With both singleton, agreement has probability 1/N. The formulas follow by summing these disjoint cases.
assumptions: integer K>=2
two independent random sets with the stated mixture law

entries.title: Switching supplies Gaussian even-moment domination
entries.statement: For a free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model on a finite graph, or its free infinite-volume limit with finitely supported nonnegative weights, let M=sum_x a_x sigma_x with a_x>=0 and V=E M^2>0. For every integer k>=1, E M^{2k}<=(2k-1)!! V^k and E exp(t M/sqrt(V))<=exp(t^2/2). In particular E(M/sqrt(V))^6<=15 and E[(M/sqrt(V))^4 1_{|M/sqrt(V)|>R}]<=15/R^2. Signed weights are not included.
entries.proof_text: In currents with sources equal to the parity set of a list of 2k spin labels and empty, the first label is connected to at least one other label: a repeated label gives a certain event, otherwise parity forces another source in its component. Switching identifies each event times the 2k-spin correlation with G(first,j) times the remaining-spin correlation. The union bound and induction give the Wick upper bound. Summing with nonnegative weights gives (2k-1)!! V^k. Spin-flip symmetry removes odd powers from the exponential; finite-volume passage proves the stated infinite-volume version. The sixth-moment tail inequality is pointwise.
assumptions: free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model
finite graph or free infinite-volume spin-correlation limit
finitely supported nonnegative weights
switching lemma for even parity source sets

entries.title: Coarse H^-2 local tightness after a smooth variance normalization
entries.statement: Let sigma be a stationary centered bounded spin field on Z^3 with nonnegative pair correlations and positive box-sum variances. Fix smooth f0 with 0<=f0<=1, f0=1 on [-1,1]^3 and support in [-2,2]^3. Let V0,L=Var(sum_x f0(x/L)sigma_x) and Phi_L=V0,L^{-1/2} sum_x sigma_x delta_{x/L} for integer L>=1. Then Phi_L is tight in H^{-2}_loc(R^3). If E[Phi_L(f0)^6]<=15 also holds, every subsequential limit Phi has E[Phi(f0)^2]=1 and is nonzero. No uniqueness, conformal invariance or sharp regularity is asserted.
entries.proof_text: Nonnegative correlations give V0,L>=Sigma_L, the variance of the radius-L box sum. Cover any fixed compact by a fixed number N of translated radius-L lattice boxes. Stationarity and Cauchy-Schwarz bound the sum-over-cover variance by N^2 Sigma_L; positive correlations then bound every bounded complex coefficient sum on that compact. Thus every Fourier coefficient of a smooth cutoff of Phi_L has a uniform second-moment bound. Summing with Sobolev weights of exponent 7/4 gives a bounded expected H^{-7/4} norm. Compact embedding into H^{-2}, Markov and a countable cutoff exhaustion give local tightness. Evaluation at f0 is continuous; the sixth-moment bound supplies uniform integrability, so variance one passes to each limit.
assumptions: stationary centered bounded lattice field in dimension three
nonnegative pair correlations
positive box-sum variance
specified smooth f0 and its own variance normalization
sixth-moment bound only for the nonzero-limit conclusion

entries.title: Source-faithful subcritical coupling from a random-root overlap
entries.statement: In the free zero-field nearest-neighbour Ising state on Z^3 at 0<beta<beta_c, write chi=sum_x G_beta(0,x)<infinity, xi>0 for the exponential correlation length and g=sum_{x,y,z}U4(0,x,y,z)/(chi^2 xi^3). Independently sample X,R with probability G_beta(0,x)/chi and single currents n,m sourced at {0,X},{0,R}, cancelling repeated labels. Put p_y=P(0 connected to y in n+tau_y m). Then -g=(2/xi^3)sum_y p_y. Let H={0,...,ceil(xi)-1}^3, N=|H|, Y uniform on H independently, W any finite set containing 0, I=|W intersect C(n,0) intersect (Y+C(m,0))|, A=E I and B=E I^2. Then A>=1/N>0 and -g>=2N A^2/(xi^3 B)>=2/(B/A^2). A bounded B/A^2 along some beta_j increasing to beta_c is therefore sufficient for the source's non-triviality definition. No such bound is proved here.
entries.proof_text: In the summed Ursell identity set z=y+r. Stationarity replaces G(y,y+r) with G(0,r). Dividing the x,r sum by chi^2 gives the two independent susceptibility endpoint draws, and nonnegative summands justify Tonelli. This proves the exact identity for -g. Restrict its root sum to H and average over Y. Single-current cluster overlap implies the original union-current connection. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds P(I>0) below by A^2/B. At Y=0 both clusters contain 0, so A>=1/N. Finally N=ceil(xi)^3>=xi^3. The ratio condition remains unproved.
assumptions: free stationary zero-field nearest-neighbour subcritical Ising state on Z^3
finite susceptibility and positive finite exponential correlation length
primary infinite-volume switching/Ursell identity
two independent susceptibility-weighted marked SINGLE currents
independent uniform root Y on the specified cube
finite W containing 0
the ratio bound is a separate unresolved input

entries.title: C0052 remaining gap: susceptibility-current overlap ratio
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT: in the sampling scheme of the source-faithful subcritical random-root criterion, find beta_j increasing to beta_c and K<infinity such that E I_beta_j^2/(E I_beta_j)^2<=K. Here the endpoints use G_beta(0,x)/chi(beta), the root shift is uniform on a cube of side ceil(xi(beta)), and the overlap uses SINGLE currents inside a finite correlation-length-scale box containing 0. Spin two-point estimates, divergent expected overlap and a lower bound for clusters enlarged with sourceless currents do not establish this bound. The critical variance-weighted block ratio is a different quantity.
assumptions: same objects, weights and normalization as the subcritical random-root criterion
clearly conjectural proof input

entries.title: Rejected route: a divergent overlap mean alone
entries.statement: INVALID GENERAL INFERENCE: two independent identically distributed nonempty random sets with divergent expected overlap must have intersection probability bounded away from zero. The rare-full-set mixture counterexample disproves this inference; a relative second-moment or other anti-concentration estimate is required before using it for an Ising non-Gaussianity argument.
assumptions: this entry records a refuted probabilistic inference, not a conjectured Ising counterexample

relations.rationale: The variance-weighted identity inserts the stated original-current Ursell identity with its original cluster event.
The overlap lower bound is converted to the exact block fourth-cumulant deficit in L002.
L004 has independent nonempty sets, E I tending to infinity, and P(I>0) tending to zero, which negates the asserted implication.
L007 uses the original infinite-volume current event and stationarity; the enlarged-cluster upper bound is excluded.
L007 gives a conditional lower bound for exactly -sum U4/(chi^2 xi^3); it does not prove the unproved ratio condition or C0052.
The gap specifies the exact root, endpoint and normalization hypotheses whose missing ratio bound would activate L007.
For the Ising application only, L005 supplies the sixth-moment assumption needed for L006's nonzero-limit conclusion; L006's tightness argument itself only uses stationary nonnegative covariance.

The existing card says 'the renormalised coupling constant does not vanish'; this source-faithful concept spells out g(beta)=sum U4/(chi^2 xi^3) and the approach from beta<beta_c, preserving UNKNOWN current status.
